ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the figure is a three-phase transformer connection diagram, with the primary side on the left in star connection and the secondary side on the right in delta connection, and the labeled line-voltage ratings are 110/220 V. The secondary side is connected to a balanced star load, with each phase resistance labeled 4Ω. The lower diagram requires this load to be equivalently referred to the primary side, forming a star equivalent load, with each phase impedance labeled Z. Reasoning: Ignoring transformer nonideal factors, the secondary-side load itself is already a balanced star pure-resistance load, so the secondary-side per-phase impedance is 4 + j0 Ω. Referring to the primary side according to the ideal transformer line-voltage ratio: Z_primary = Z_secondary × (110/220)^2 = 4 × (1/2)^2 = 1 Ω. Since the load is pure resistance, the imaginary part is 0. Therefore the primary-side equivalent star per-phase impedance is 1 + j0 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note the Y primary, Δ secondary, and the 4 Ω star-connected load at the secondary terminals. Convert the secondary star load to an equivalent delta load across the secondary line terminals: each delta branch is 3×4 = 12 Ω.
